title: Periodic Quarter-Wave Bragg Stack for 8-13 μm High Emissivity
scientific_hypothesis: A periodic alternating HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave stack tuned to the center of the 8-13 μm atmospheric window will produce high emissivity in that band through constructive interference while suppressing emissivity in the 3-5 μm band through destructive interference.
design_principle: Quarter-wave optical thickness layers create a photonic bandgap where reflectance is minimized (emissivity maximized) at the design wavelength and its harmonics. By centering the stack at ~10.5 μm, the fundamental resonance falls within the atmospheric window while the 3-5 μm band lies outside the high-emissivity region.
proposed_topology: air | (hfo2 | sio2)_6 | si substrate, exactly 12 layers total (6 pairs)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 12 layers, starting from quarter-wave at 10500 nm center wavelength
soft_objectives: maximize mean emissivity in 8000-13000 nm band
minimize mean emissivity in 3000-5000 nm band
maintain total layer count at exactly 12
manufacturing_considerations: 12 layers is well within the 24-layer limit
quarter-wave thicknesses at 10.5 μm are physically realizable (hundreds of nm to microns)
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard deposition materials
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
Kirchhoff's law relating emissivity to absorptance
expected_advantages: Simple periodic structure is easy to fabricate
Literature L16 and L20 support multilayer selective emitter approach
known_risks: Periodic stacks produce narrowband response that may not cover full 8-13 μm window
Higher-order harmonics could create unwanted emissivity peaks in 3-5 μm band
Fixed pair count may limit achievable selectivity
execution_request_english: Design a periodic multilayer dielectric stack on silicon substrate with air incidence. Stack structure: air | (hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat))_6 | si, exactly 12 layers total. Optimize individual layer thicknesses for all 12 layers, initialized at quarter-wave optical thickness for 10500 nm center wavelength. Target: maximize emissivity in 8000-13000 nm band, minimize emissivity in 3000-5000 nm band. Wavelength range for evaluation: 3000-13000 nm. Polarization: unpolarized (average TE and TM). Incidence angle: 0 degrees (normal). Material refractive indices from catalog datasets for hfo2, SiO2 (Kischkat), and si. Total layer count fixed at 12.
